news.title: AI leaders called for a slowdown, and the money that builds AI got repriced
news.summary: Anthropic's Dario Amodei published an essay arguing the pace of frontier AI development should slow, and OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk publicly agreed. No filing, no rule, no guidance change — a positioning statement. The tape treated it as a direct hit to committed chip and datacenter spending. Overnight: SK Hynix -6%, Samsung Electronics -4%, SoftBank -10%. Premarket in the capex chain: Nebius -8.7%, CoreWeave -8.4%, Marvell -8.4%, Arm -7.7%, Intel -6.7%, Micron -6.6%, AMD -5.8%, Oracle -5.0%, Nvidia -2.7%. The AI-datacenter power names went with them: Oklo -3.6%, Constellation -3.0%, Vistra -2.8%. Volatility gave back Friday's collapse, with the VIX back to 17.65 from a 15.84 close.

news.title: It is not a tech selloff — the companies that use AI are green
news.summary: The split is the whole story. While the builders sold off, the platforms and applications rallied premarket: ServiceNow +5.0%, Adobe +3.7%, Alphabet +1.7%, Meta +1.7%, Apple +0.8%, Microsoft +0.7%. Enterprise software with no capex exposure led the liquid gainer list alongside them — HubSpot, Atlassian, SAP, Accenture, Asana. One index line carries it: the Nasdaq proxy is down roughly 2.4 times the S&P proxy, with the Dow proxy nearly flat and small caps barely moved. That is a concentrated repricing of one spending chain, not broad risk-off.

news.title: Cybersecurity is the bid side of the same headline
news.summary: Security names rallied hard on the argument that an AI-risk narrative means companies spend more on protection, not less: CrowdStrike +7.4%, Palo Alto Networks +5.4%, Zscaler +4.8%, SentinelOne +4.4%, Okta +3.7%, Cloudflare +2.8%. The framing feeds off Jensen Huang's comment last Thursday that cybersecurity is likely AI's next major growth market, and Anthropic's disclosure that it disrupted a Russia-linked campaign using its models against more than 20 Ukrainian government and defense targets. None of these names has an earnings catalyst today — the move is entirely the headline.

news.title: Oil's war premium came back over the weekend, bigger than before
news.summary: This reverses Friday's de-escalation story outright. Saudi Arabia shut its main East-West pipeline — the Red Sea route that bypasses Hormuz — after drone strikes near key pumping stations. A merchant vessel was struck in the Strait of Hormuz and one crew member was killed. The Iran-Gulf talks on a temporary shipping corridor, the headline that knocked $3 out of crude on Friday, were postponed. Brent crossed $108, a four-month high, up more than 3%; WTI is near $102. The shut pipeline was moving roughly 7 million barrels a day, and reporting suggests Saudi exportable inventory could be drawn down within days if it is not restarted. Energy equities followed: the oil fund +2.9%, Exxon +1.8%, Chevron +1.6%, Occidental +2.2%.

news.title: Wednesday's Fed decision is now priced as a hike, not a hold
news.summary: After Friday's hotter-than-expected August CPI — +0.4% month-over-month, +3.4% year-over-year, core +0.3% against roughly +0.2% expected — market-implied odds of a quarter-point rate hike at Wednesday's meeting sit near 85%, with another increasingly expected before year-end. The decision lands at 2:00 PM ET Wednesday with the press conference at 2:30. Retail sales print the same morning at 8:30. Notably, small caps are down less than half a percent despite that, so the hike is not what is moving the tape today.

news.title: Crypto is sitting this one out, except for the miners
news.summary: Spot is flat and quiet: Bitcoin near $78,300 (+0.8% since midnight ET), Ether near $2,504 (-0.4%), Solana near $101.56 (+0.4%). Majors are inside half a percent and conspicuously not participating in the equity selloff. The exception is the miners, and it is not a crypto story — Marathon -6.8% and Riot -5.3% premarket while Bitcoin was green and the spot ETF proxy tracked it cleanly at +0.6%. Both have been repriced over the past year as AI and high-performance-computing datacenter hosts, so the frontier-slowdown headline hits their compute-demand leg while the mining leg goes nowhere. Coinbase diverged the other way at +2.1% with no name-specific news found.
